title: package-result (EXPERIMENTAL, schemaVersion 1)
description: One apex-sentinel pkg-check.py run on one app and one environment: the packages and procedures the change names (an invokeApi process or workflow activity, or a named-notation call in a sql/plsql block of the .apx) looked up, with read-only SELECTs, in the app's parsing schema. Written by the tool (method: tool) to stdout and, with --task, to <evidenceDir>/<task>/package-<alias>[.<env>].json. Advisories never change the status. A PASS is never 'the PL/SQL is right': the objects exist, are VALID and have no compile errors in that database, when the run read it.

database.description: What the queries ran as and against: the session's user, and the app's parsing schema (apex_applications.owner) the names were looked up in.

unparsed.description: Files, or processes inside them, the reader could not follow (an owner, a remote database, an invoke.type it does not know, a parse error): what they name was not looked up. The line is in the detail.

advisories.description: ADVISE signals (PKG-STANDALONE: an invokeApi process that names a standalone procedure or function, not looked up): reported, never a verdict.

evidence.description: The SELECTs that ran, each with its exit code and the number of rows it returned.

allOf.description: PASS: the three criteria held, on at least one package and one procedure, and none is FAIL or UNKNOWN
a FAIL criterion makes the run FAIL
a verdict names the database it read: the app, the connection, the owner and the session
a PASS read source files and parsed every one
a PASS rests on a query that ran: a SELECT that exited 0

identifier.description: An Oracle identifier, upper-cased, as it is looked up: never free text.

status.description: UNKNOWN: looked up, and the answer reads neither as held nor as failed. NOT_RUN: nothing to look up.

allOf.description: a criterion not exercised says why
a FAIL or an UNKNOWN names what it is about; a PASS has nothing against it

finding.description: Where the name comes from (path, line) and what the lookup said: never source text, a connect string or a value.
